title: Site comparison preserves the support localization boundary
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $A$ a finite commutative ring. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $i:C\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $j:V=T\setminus C\hookrightarrow T$ be its open complement [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $F$ be an ordinary sheaf of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on the small etale site, viewed in degree zero in $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $F_p=\nu_T^*F$; identify $j^{-1}F_p$ with $\nu_V^*(j^{-1}F)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback].

Let $c_T^q$ and $c_V^q$ be the degree-$q$ global-section comparison maps induced by the derived adjunction unit [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology]. Let $c_C^q$ be the degree-$q$ map of the canonical support comparison $c^C_{T,F}$ of [lem-pur-support-site-comparison], with supported cohomology defined by the kernel-of-restriction right derived functor [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Let $\partial_{\mathrm{et}}^q$ and $\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}^q$ be the connecting maps of the two support long exact sequences [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], using the same cochain/snake-boundary convention in the two topologies. Then the triples $(c_C^q,c_T^q,c_V^q)$ form a morphism between these long exact sequences. In particular, for every $q\geq0$,
$$
c_C^{q+1}\circ\partial_{\mathrm{et}}^q
=\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}^q\circ c_V^q:
H^q(V_{\mathrm{et}},j^{-1}F)\longrightarrow
H^{q+1}_C(T_{\mathrm{proet}},F_p).
$$
All squares, including the restriction and forgetting-supports squares, commute without an additional sign. These maps and squares are natural in $A_T$-linear morphisms of $F$; in particular all comparison maps and connecting maps are $A$-linear. No constructibility or freeness assumption is imposed on $F$.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-support-comparison-common-injectives], choose $h:F_p\to J^\bullet$ and the etale resolution $a:F\to I^\bullet=\nu_{T,*}J^\bullet$. The section complexes on $T,V$ and their support kernels are identified termwise, including differentials, inclusions and restrictions.

source.place: Tag 099V, label lemma-relative-comparison, clause (2), and Tag 09B1, label lemma-compare-derived, clause (2). Agent-formulated injective-model refinement: resolution existence, preservation of injectives by the right adjoint, and the specified augmentation are extracted from old proof steps 1-2 of lem-pur-support-comparison-boundary.

proof.text: Each term $E$ of either resolution is an injective sheaf of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A$ on the small etale, respectively pro-etale, site. The open immersion $j:V\to T$ is a monomorphism in that site, so [lem-pur-ringed-site-injective-mono-restriction] makes the restriction $E(T)\to E(V)$ surjective. Thus $0\to\ker(E^\bullet(T)\to E^\bullet(V))\to E^\bullet(T)\to E^\bullet(V)\to0$ is degreewise short exact, with $A$-linear arrows.

source.place: Tag 093X, label lemma-restriction-along-monomorphism-surjective (restriction of an injective O-module along a monomorphism is surjective), as used in etale-cohomology.tex Tag 09XP.

proof.text: The kernel and middle complexes compute derived supports [def-pur-support-cohomology, lem-pur-support-site-comparison] and global sections. Open restriction preserves injective module sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives, lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives], so the last complexes compute cohomology of $V$. The two rows therefore give the localization sequences of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], with the stipulated snake convention. Finiteness of $A$ makes all coefficient sheaves torsion; no finiteness of section modules is needed.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support, injective restriction sequence; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03F3, lemma-cohomology-of-open, and Section 03FA, cohomology of modules.

proof.text: The termwise identities give a morphism of these short exact complexes. By [lem-pur-support-comparison-section-model], its three cohomology components are exactly $c_C^q,c_T^q,c_V^q$, with the specified open coefficient identification and augmentations.

source.place: Tag 09XP, label section-cohomology-support, kernel restriction construction. Agent-formulated refinement identifying the three etale/pro-etale comparison components on the common injective model (old proof step 5 of lem-pur-support-comparison-boundary), with open-unit compatibility made explicit; the tag alone does not assert site-comparison normalization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] to this morphism of short exact complexes. The result is a morphism of the full long exact sequences, with $c_C^{q+1}\partial_{\mathrm{et}}^q=\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}^q c_V^q$. To see the sign explicitly, a cocycle on $V$ is lifted to a cochain on $T$, its differential lies in the support kernel, and the class of this differential is the connecting image. The termwise identifications send the chosen lift and its differential to the same cochains in the other row. Both boundaries therefore give the same class, with no negation. Naturality of the comparisons in [lem-pur-support-site-comparison] and [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology], and coefficient functoriality of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], give naturality of all these squares in $F$. All complexes and their arrows are $A$-linear, so their induced cohomology and connecting maps are $A$-linear as well.

source.place: Tag 0117, lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain; Tag 08N7, lemma-snake-natural. The explicit lift-and-differentiate computation uses the same boundary convention in both rows.
